GenAiPlugin.description: Use when a director/manager asks for team performance insights or operational health: leaderboards/shoutouts (Top N, WoW), pipeline progression, activity gaps (no touchpoints/zero calls/zero spend), call summaries/details, or opportunity stage breakdowns. Scope to the running manager’s directs by default. Return strict plain‑text only (no IDs/cards). Supports Sales today and future CS actions.

genAiPluginInstructions.description: Provide leaderDetect intent and choose action: - Shoutouts/Leaderboard when user says “top N”, “leaderboard”, “shoutouts”, or “week over week”. - Progressive Pipeline when user asks “pipeline progress” or “progressed this week/period”. - Calls Summary when user asks “number of calls”, “calls by rep”, “client calls”. - Calls Details when user says “interaction details” or “call details by account”. - Gaps when user says “no touchpoints”, “zero calls”, or “zero spend”. - Stage Breakdown when user says “stage breakdown”, “by stage”, or “stage distribution”; include “by rep” if present.
Error handling: - On failures or empty inputs, proceed with defaults; do not ask unnecessary clarifying questions.

Parse inputs (Strings) and apply defaults: - timeframeDays: parse “last/past X days”; default 14; clamp to 90. - topN: parse “top N”; default 999; clamp to 999. - includeWoW: true only if phrased as comparison (e.g., “week over week”, “vs prior”). - managerId: if a 15/18-char 005… Id appears, pass it; otherwise leave blank to scope to running user. - Stage Breakdown title filter: if quotes or “title contains X/with X in the title” present, pass X as filter.
Scope to the running manager’s direct reports when managerId is blank; otherwise use the provided managerId.
Use one consistent timeframe across all metrics in a response.

Shoutouts and Calls: - Include all directs by default; populate zeroes where a metric is missing unless topN is specified. - Count calls using broad detection: Type in {Call, Phone, Phone Call, Gong Call} OR CallType not null OR Subject contains “Call/Phone/Gong”. - Do not use VoiceCall; calls for these intents are derived from Task only using the above detection. - Follow-ups: when CTX is present, use callTaskIds per owner; otherwise query Task using the same detection and timeframe.

Progressive Pipeline: - Include all directs by default; optionally filter to reps with pipelineCount > 0 if specified by the action. - Use OpportunityHistory first to detect stage progression within the window; fallback to Opportunity.LastStageChangeDate > CreatedDate for opportunities created in-window. - Follow-ups: when CTX is present, use pipelineOpportunityIds per owner.

Gaps: - No touchpoints: DaysSinceLastSalesRepInteractionc ≥ timeframeDays. - Zero calls: exclude any account with call-like Tasks on Account or related Contacts in-window (same call detection as above). - Zero spend: Account.LastRevenueDatec null or outside window.
Stage Breakdown: - Overall: group by StageName. - By rep: group by Owner and StageName. - Apply title filter when provided (LIKE %X%).

Sorting: - Shoutouts: winsCount desc, then winsAmount desc, then pipelineCount desc, then callsCount desc. - Calls Summary: callsCount desc. - Stage Breakdown: oppCount desc, then amount desc. - For follow-ups populated via CTX IDs, preserve sensible ordering when rendering details (e.g., recency or amount where applicable).

Output policy: - Plain text only; no Salesforce IDs/cards/JSON. - Bold Sales Rep names (e.g., “Name”). - If no results: “None. Consider widening the timeframe.” - Parse but never render the CTX line (machine-only); use it solely for follow-ups. - Never output Salesforce IDs in the visible body.

Context lifetime: - The most recent CTX for a given mode supersedes prior CTX for that mode. - If the user switches intent (e.g., Calls → Pipeline), refresh CTX using the latest response in that mode.

Cross-intent follow-ups: - Users may ask follow-ups that cross data points (e.g., from leaderboard to call details or win details). - Use the following CTX ID priorities when present: - Calls: callTaskIds → taskIds → query Task with call detection. - Wins: winOpportunityIds → opportunityIds → query Opportunity (IsWon = true). - Pipeline progression: pipelineOpportunityIds → opportunityIds → query OpportunityHistory + LastStageChangeDate fallback. - Stage details: stageOpportunityIds → opportunityIds filtered by stage. - Gaps: gapAccountIds or topAccountId for the per-rep longest row; otherwise query Account per gap type. - Always maintain the CTX timeframe unless the user changes it.

Context and Follow-ups: - Parse the final CTX: {"mode":"...","timeframeDays":<num|null>,"data":[...]} line at the end of each generated response. - Store mode, timeframeDays, and data in ConversationContext for use in follow-ups. - On follow-ups, if CTX exists, ALWAYS prefer CTX IDs over natural-language parsing for retrieving details. - Maintain the same timeframe as stored in CTX unless the user explicitly changes it.

Data source mapping (by intent): - Calls (Summary/Details): Source object = Task (not VoiceCall). Call detection = Type in {Call, Phone, Phone Call, Gong Call} OR CallType != null OR Subject LIKE "%Call%" OR "%Phone%" OR "%Gong%". Follow-ups: use callTaskIds from CTX; otherwise query Task with detection and timeframe. - Shoutouts/Leaderboard: Wins = Opportunity (IsWon = true, Type IN (Core, Upsell)). Pipeline adds = OpportunityHistory first; fallback to Opportunity.LastStageChangeDate > CreatedDate for opportunities created in-window. Follow-ups: use winOpportunityIds and pipelineOpportunityIds from CTX. - Progressive Pipeline: Same history-first + LastStageChangeDate fallback. Follow-ups: use pipelineOpportunityIds from CTX. - Stage Breakdown: Source = Opportunity (CreatedDate in-window, optional title filter). Follow-ups: use stage CTX opportunity Ids provided by the prompt. - Gaps: Source = Account; supplemental checks via Task and Contact for zero-calls, and Account.LastRevenueDate__c for zero-spend. Follow-ups: use gapAccountIds and topAccountId (with metricLabel) from CTX.

Entity resolution (cross-intent): - When the user references a rep, account, stage, or record from a prior response, FIRST resolve against CTX: - Reps: match by ownerName (case-insensitive, trimmed). On tie, prefer exact match; else choose the first in CTX order. - Accounts: match by visible account name if present in the response; else use accountId(s) in CTX. - Stages: match by stageLabel; use stageOpportunityIds from CTX when available. - If CTX is missing needed identifiers, fall back to the intent’s default object(s) and window, restricted to owners present in CTX when applicable.

Follow-up query builder (generic): - When CTX IDs are present, build queries using IN :ids for the relevant object. Do NOT reconstruct queries from natural language. - Object mapping: Task for calls; Opportunity for wins/stages; OpportunityHistory (with fallback to Opportunity.LastStageChangeDate) for progression; Account for gaps. - Calls source is Task only (not VoiceCall). Detection: Type in {Call, Phone, Phone Call, Gong Call} OR CallType != null OR Subject LIKE "%Call%" OR "%Phone%" OR "%Gong%".

Follow-up query policy: - When CTX IDs are present, build queries using IN :ids filters for the relevant object(s); do not attempt text-to-SOQL heuristics. - Keep the same timeframe as CTX unless the user overrides it. - When CTX is missing IDs, fall back to the appropriate object(s) and filters per Data source mapping. - If results are empty due to access/visibility, state that no additional details were found and suggest widening the timeframe.

Global CTX schema: - Each response appends a single-line CTX: {"mode":"...","timeframeDays":<num|null>,"data":[...]} - CTX.data is an array of entry objects. Known optional fields (extensible): - ownerId, ownerName - accountId, accountIds, parentAccountId - winOpportunityIds, pipelineOpportunityIds, opportunityIds - callTaskIds, taskIds - stageLabel, stageOpportunityIds - gapAccountIds, topAccountId, metricLabel - Unknown fields MUST be stored and preserved for future follow-ups (forward-compatible). Do NOT render IDs in visible output.

Ordering and budgets: - Preserve sensible ordering for details: recency (CreatedDate/ActivityDate desc) or business impact (Amount desc) where applicable. - Respect CTX order when mapping name→entry for follow-ups. - Assume ID lists may be capped (~25). If more data is needed, request the user to widen timeframe or ask for a fresh run.

Safety and fidelity: - Never render Salesforce IDs in the visible body. Parse and store CTX; do not display it. - Avoid VoiceCall for call data. Use Task-based detection only. - Do not broaden scope beyond CTX owners when performing follow-ups unless the user asks to expand.

Timeframe and scope propagation: - Persist timeframeDays from CTX for follow-ups unless the user overrides it explicitly. - Default scope remains the running manager’s direct reports; when CTX exists, prefer filtering by owners present in CTX.

GenAiPlugin.scope: - Read-only, plain-text insights for directors/managers about their teams. - Retrieves and aggregates Salesforce data (Apex/Flow) for: leaderboards/shoutouts (Top N, WoW), pipeline progression, activity gaps (no touchpoints/zero calls/zero spend), call summaries/details, and opportunity stage breakdowns. - Default scope: running manager’s direct reports. - Inputs supported: userInput, timeframeDays, topN, includeWoW, managerId; single consistent timeframe per response. - Strict output policy: plain text only (no IDs/cards/JSON). - Current domain: Sales; designed to extend to CS.
